facts: Terminology structuring has been the subject of much work in the context of terms extracted from corpora.
A set of terms can be extracted from a corpus.
Terminology structuring identifies hierarchical relations between terms.
The present paper focuses on terminology structuring by lexical methods.
Lexical methods match terms on the basis of their content words.
Lexical methods take morphological variants into account.
Experiments are done on a 'flat' list of terms.
The 'flat' list of terms is obtained from an originally hierarchically-structured terminology.
The originally hierarchically-structured terminology is the French version of the US National Library of Medicine MeSH thesaurus.
The study compares the lexically-induced relations with the original MeSH relations.
A quantitative evaluation of congruence is done through recall and precision metrics.
A qualitative, human analysis is performed of the 'new' relations not present in the MeSH.
The analysis shows the limits of the lexical structuring method.
The analysis reveals some specific structuring choices and naming conventions made by the MeSH designers.
The analysis emphasizes ontological commitments that can not be left to automatic structuring.
